manifest.title: PostgreSQL Server
manifest.author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
manifest.description:
## About

A standalone PostgreSQL 18 server for clients outside of Cloudron, with a web panel to manage roles and databases.

* Connections are TLS 1.3 only, using the app domain's certificate
* Passwords use SCRAM-SHA-256 and are generated by the panel
* Remote access is blocked until a network is added to the allowlist
* Each role only gets access to the databases it owns
* Sign in with Cloudron. Admins manage roles, databases and allowed networks. Roles are owned by Cloudron users and groups, every owner has an own login
* Users can create, download and restore snapshots of their databases
* Users can upload pg_dump archives and import them into their databases
* Backups are logical dumps taken by Cloudron's backup, snapshots stay on the server and are not part of them
manifest.tagline: Standalone PostgreSQL server reachable from external hosts

create-admin-group.message: Set admins: add Cloudron usernames to PG_ADMINS in /app/data/env.sh, or add users to a Cloudron group named postgres-admins. Restart the app after editing env.sh.

POSTGRES_PORT.title: PostgreSQL Port
POSTGRES_PORT.description: Port for PostgreSQL client connections (TLS only)

manifest.changelog:
* Initial version with PostgreSQL 18.6
* Remote access over TLS 1.3 with SCRAM-SHA-256, blocked until a network is added to the allowlist
* Admin panel with Cloudron login: roles, databases, allowed networks, audit log
* Roles are owned by Cloudron users and groups. Every owner has an own login, it is removed when the user is no longer an owner
* Owners can create databases up to a limit set by the admin
* Snapshots on demand and on a schedule, download as .dump or .sql, restore into a staging database that is swapped in
* Import of uploaded pg_dump archives with SHA-256 checks
* Progress display for snapshots, restores and imports
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Remote connections are blocked until you allow a network.

1. Make yourself an admin: set `PG_ADMINS="<your username>"` in `/app/data/env.sh` and restart the app, or add yourself to a Cloudron group named `postgres-admins`.
2. Open the app, sign in, and go to **Admin**.
3. Add the IP address of your client server under **Allowed networks**.
4. Create a role and choose its owners (Cloudron users and groups).
5. Each owner signs in, opens **My databases** and creates an own password. It is shown once and not stored.
6. Connect with TLS verification, using your login `<role>.<username>`:
   `psql "postgresql://<role>.<username>:<password>@$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN:<port>/<database>?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=system"`
   On Windows, `sslrootcert=system` does not find the Windows certificate store. Download [isrgrootx1.pem](https://letsencrypt.org/certs/isrgrootx1.pem) and pass its path instead.

manifest.changelog:
* New panel design: icon buttons with optional labels, settings in sheets, a bottom navigation bar on phones
* Snapshot, restore and import progress updates live, without reloading the page
* Failure mails are opt-in: each user turns them on in the account settings. Owners no longer get them automatically
* Admins can change selected PostgreSQL settings (max_connections, memory and timeouts) in Admin > Server
* Admin overview links to lists of all client connections and all snapshots

* Users can upload pg_dump archives and import them into their databases
* Users can turn on mails about failed snapshots, restores and imports
* Admins can change selected PostgreSQL settings such as max_connections and work_mem
* Backups are logical dumps taken by Cloudron's backup, snapshots stay on the server and are not part of them
manifest.tagline: Standalone PostgreSQL server reachable from external hosts

create-admin-group.message: Set admins: add Cloudron usernames to PG_ADMINS or Cloudron groups to PG_ADMIN_GROUP in /app/data/env.sh. Restart the app after editing env.sh.

POSTGRES_PORT.title: PostgreSQL Port
POSTGRES_PORT.description: Port for PostgreSQL client connections (TLS only)

manifest.postInstallMessage:
Remote connections are blocked until you allow a network.

1. Make yourself an admin: set `PG_ADMINS="<your username>"` in `/app/data/env.sh` and restart the app. To make the members of Cloudron groups admins, list the groups in `PG_ADMIN_GROUP`, separated by commas.
2. Open the app, sign in, and go to **Admin**.
3. Add the IP address of your client server under **Admin > Network**.
4. Create a role under **Admin > Roles** and choose its owners (Cloudron users and groups).
5. Each owner signs in, opens the role settings (gear icon) on **My databases** and creates an own password. It is shown once and not stored.
6. Connect with TLS verification, using your login `<role>.<username>`:
   `psql "postgresql://<role>.<username>:<password>@$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN:<port>/<database>?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=system"`
   On Windows, `sslrootcert=system` does not find the Windows certificate store. Download [isrgrootx1.pem](https://letsencrypt.org/certs/isrgrootx1.pem) and pass its path instead.
